{{2025–26 ACC men's basketball standings}}
The '''2025–26 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Louisville]] during the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team played its home games on Denny Crum Court at the [[KFC Yum! Center]] in [[Downtown Louisville|downtown Louisville, Kentucky]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). They were led by second-year head coach [[Pat Kelsey]].

The Cardinals began the season with seven straight wins, which saw them rise from eleventh in the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings|AP poll]] to sixth. The run included two games against Power 4 opponents. The first was a 96–88 victory over [[Kentucky–Louisville rivalry|rivals]] and ninth-ranked [[2025–26 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]]. The second was a ten-point win over [[Cincinnati–Louisville rivalry#Men's Basketball|rivals]] [[2025–26 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]]. Their streak was broken in the [[ACC–SEC Challenge]] at twenty-fifth ranked [[2025–26 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]], where they lost by nine points. The team followed the loss with a victory in the CareSource Invitational over twenty-second ranked [[2025–26 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]]. The win was not enough to prevent them from sliding back to eleventh in the AP poll. They defeated [[Louisville–Memphis rivalry|rivals]] [[2025–26 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|Memphis]] 99–73 before losing 62–83 at twentieth-ranked [[2025–26 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]]. The Cardinals defeated [[2025–26 Montana Grizzlies basketball team|Montana]] before falling to sixteenth in the AP poll to begin ACC play. They went 2–3 in their first five games, winning the opener at [[2025–26 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]] and defeating [[2025–26 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College]] but losing to sixth-ranked [[2025–26 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]], sixteenth-ranked [[2025–26 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]], and at [[2025–26 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|Stanford]]. The team went 5–1 over their next six games, with the only loss coming to fourth-ranked Duke. On February 9, 2026, Mikel Brown Jr. broke the ACC Freshman scoring record and tied the Louisville program 59-year scoring record with 45 points in a 118–77 win against [[2025-26 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]].  [[Ryan Conwell]] added 31 points marking the first 30-point scoring duo in program history.<ref name="45point">{{cite web |title=Brown Jr. Breaks ACC Freshman Scoring Record, Ties Program Record in 118-77 Rout of NC State |url=https://gocards.com/news/2026/2/9/mens-basketball-brown-jr-breaks-acc-freshman-scoring-record-ties-program-record-in-118-77-rout-of-nc-state |website=Go Cards |publisher=University of Louisville |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=9 February 2026}}</ref><ref name="45espn">{{cite web |title=Louisville 118-77 NC State (Feb 9, 2026) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401820730 |website=ESPN |access-date=16 February 2026}}</ref> Despite the winning streak, the Cardinals feel to twenty fourth in the AP poll by the end of the run. They defeated [[2025–26 Baylor Bears men's basketball team|Baylor]] 82–71 at a neutral site to move up to twenty-first, but lost three of their next four games to fall out of the rankings. They only defeated [[2025–26 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]] while losing at [[2025–26 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|SMU]], at [[2025–26 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]], and at eighteenth-ranked [[2025–26 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]]. They finished their regular season with defeats of [[2025–26 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] and twenty-second ranked [[2025–26 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]].

The Cardinals finished the season 24–11 overall and 11–7 in [[2025–26 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a sixth place. As the sixth seed in the [[2026 ACC men's basketball tournament|2026 ACC tournament]], they earned a bye into the Second Round where they defeated SMU by four points. Their run ended there as they lost to Miami in a re-match of their final regular season game. The Cardinals earned an at-large bid to the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and were the six-seed in the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#East regional – Washington, D.C.|East region]]. They defeated eleven-seed [[2025–26 South Florida Bulls men's basketball team|South Florida]] in the First Round before losing to third-seed and eleventh ranked [[2025–26 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] in the Second Round to end their season.

==Previous season==
The [[2024–25 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Cardinals]] finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25 season]] with a record of 27–8, 18–2 in [[2024–25 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]], finishing in a tie for 2nd place. As the second seed in the [[2025 ACC men's basketball tournament|2025 ACC tournament]] they earned a bye into Quarterfinals where they defeated seventh seed Stanford for the second time in five days. The tournament game was much closer as the Cardinals advanced 75–73.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Louisville basketball rallies vs Stanford in ACC Tournament quarterfinal on buzzer-beater |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2025/03/13/louisville-stanford-score-acc-tournament-bracket-update/78990167007/ |website=Courier-Journal |access-date=2025-10-14}}</ref> In the Semifinals they defeated third seed and tenth-ranked [[2024–25 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]] 76–73.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Crawford: Louisville holds on to beat Clemson 76–73, gets Duke in ACC title game |url=https://www.wdrb.com/sports/crawford-louisville-holds-on-to-beat-clemson-76-73-gets-duke-in-acc-title-game/article_97829c42-0155-11f0-b484-0bff98cc9470.html |website=WDRB |date=March 15, 2025 |access-date=2025-10-14}}</ref> They lost to first seed and top ranked Duke 73–62 in the final.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Duke 73-62 Louisville (Mar 15, 2025) |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game/_/gameId/401743776/louisville-duke |website=ESPN |access-date=2025-10-14}}</ref> They received an at-large bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a No. 8 seed, where they lost in the first round to [[2024–25 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Louisville vs. Creighton score, bracket update (March Madness) |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2025/03/20/louisville-creighton-score-march-madness-bracket-update-ncaa/80067504007/ |website=Courier-Journal |access-date=2025-10-14}}</ref>
